topic_description: transformer-based incremental object detection with knowledge distillation and exemplar replay on COCO dataset

Dynamic Exemplar Composition for Increme.Problem: Incremental object detection suffers from catastrophic forgetting when learning new classes, especially when exemplars from previous classes are limited or unavailable.
Dynamic Exemplar Composition for Increme.Existing Methods: Current approaches often rely on fixed exemplar sets or knowledge distillation, which can be inefficient or insufficient for preserving old knowledge.
Dynamic Exemplar Composition for Increme.Motivation: Inspired by how humans compose and synthesize memories, we propose a method to dynamically generate and refine exemplars that capture the essence of old classes while being compatible with new class learning.
Dynamic Exemplar Composition for Increme.Proposed Method: We introduce Dynamic Exemplar Composition (DEC), a novel approach that leverages the transformer architecture to create synthetic exemplars. DEC consists of three key components: 1) A memory bank that stores compressed representations of old class features. 2) An exemplar generator transformer that takes the memory bank and new class data as input to synthesize diverse and informative exemplars. 3) An adaptive refinement module that iteratively updates the synthetic exemplars based on their effectiveness in preserving old knowledge and facilitating new class learning. The exemplar generator uses cross-attention mechanisms to fuse old and new class information, creating exemplars that maintain old class characteristics while being compatible with the evolving feature space. The adaptive refinement module evaluates exemplar quality using a meta-learning approach, adjusting exemplar composition to maximize performance on both old and new classes.
Dynamic Exemplar Composition for Increme.Experiment Plan: We will evaluate DEC on the COCO dataset using standard incremental object detection protocols. Baselines will include fixed exemplar replay methods and knowledge distillation approaches. We will measure performance using mean Average Precision (mAP) across all classes, as well as forgetting and intransigence metrics to assess preservation of old knowledge and acquisition of new classes. Ablation studies will be conducted to analyze the impact of each component in the DEC framework.

Multi-Scale Attention Alignment for Tran.Problem: Transformer-based object detectors struggle to maintain consistent attention patterns across incremental learning stages, leading to degraded performance on both old and new classes.
Multi-Scale Attention Alignment for Tran.Existing Methods: Existing methods often focus on feature-level or output-level knowledge distillation, neglecting the importance of preserving attention mechanisms in transformer architectures.
Multi-Scale Attention Alignment for Tran.Motivation: The self-attention mechanism is crucial for transformer-based detectors. By aligning attention patterns across incremental stages, we can better preserve the model's ability to focus on relevant object features for both old and new classes.
Multi-Scale Attention Alignment for Tran.Proposed Method: We propose Multi-Scale Attention Alignment (MSAA), a novel approach for incremental object detection that focuses on preserving and adapting attention patterns. MSAA consists of: 1) A hierarchical attention distillation module that aligns attention maps at multiple scales, from low-level features to high-level semantic representations. 2) An adaptive attention fusion mechanism that combines old and new class attention patterns, allowing for gradual adaptation of attention. 3) A contrastive attention learning objective that encourages discriminative attention patterns between classes. The hierarchical attention distillation uses a pyramid structure to capture and align attention at different abstraction levels. The adaptive fusion mechanism employs a gating network to determine the optimal combination of old and new attention patterns. The contrastive learning objective pushes the model to learn class-specific attention patterns that are distinct yet coherent across incremental stages.
Multi-Scale Attention Alignment for Tran.Experiment Plan: We will evaluate MSAA on the COCO dataset using various incremental learning scenarios. Baselines will include state-of-the-art incremental object detection methods and transformer-based detectors without incremental learning capabilities. We will measure performance using mAP, attention consistency metrics, and visualization of attention maps. Additional experiments will assess the method's robustness to different incremental class distributions and its generalization to other transformer architectures.
